title: Tadla irrigated plain, Beni Moussa side, 16 Jul to 14 Sep 2026
summary: From 16 Jul to 14 Sep 2026 the radar shows 7.92 km2 turning brighter and 5.83 km2 darker in HV on the Tadla plain, inside the 9 km circle. Most of the brighter area, 5.39 km2, is on the changing fields.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 60 days mean HV moved by 0.14 dB and mean HH by 0.49 dB. In HV, 7.92 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 5.83 km2 darker; in HH, 17.68 km2 turned brighter and 5.49 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The changing fields had 5.39 km2 brighter and 4.12 km2 darker in HV, with a mean HV change of 0.47 dB. Rough dry ground and fields had 1.78 km2 brighter and 1.13 km2 darker in HV. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes changed by 0.11 dB in HV, and built-up land by 0.31 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the brighter fields: new crops sown after the summer harvest, which add volume scattering; sowing records or a field visit would confirm it. Possible cause for the darker fields: plots harvested or ploughed; the optical photo would show them. Possible cause for part of the HH rise, built-up land included: a small calibration difference between the acquisitions; stable targets on more dates would check it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen. One track only, so field edges facing away from the radar can look darker.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: An irrigation office could compare the 5.39 km2 of brighter fields with its sowing and water-delivery records, since these plots are growing a crop now.
